prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

They flee from me, that sometime did me seek With naked foot, stalking in my chamber. I have seen them gentle, tame, and meek, That now are wild, and do not remember That sometime they put themselves in danger To take bread at my hand; and now they range Busily seeking with a continual change. Thanked be fortune it hath been otherwise Twenty times better; but once, in special, In thin array, after a pleasant guise, When her loose gown from her shoulders did fall, And she me caught in her arms long and small; Therewith all sweetly did me kiss, And softly said, ‘Dear heart, how like you this?’ It was no dream: I lay broad waking: But all is turned, thorough my gentleness, Into a strange fashion of forsaking; And I have leave to go of her goodness, And she also to use newfangleness. But since that I so kindly am served, I would fain know what she hath deserved.

prompts.L5:
Please write a text about the following topic:

Keywords: They, With, That

outputs.L1:
They flee from me who once did seek me out,  
Barefoot, stalking softly through my chamber.  
I have seen them gentle, tame, and meek,  
Who now run wild and no longer remember  
How once they placed themselves in danger  
To take bread from my hand; now they roam,  
Busily seeking, ever drawn to change.

Thanks be to fortune, it has been otherwise—  
Twenty times better—but once, above all,  
She came lightly clad, in pleasing fashion,  
Her loose gown falling from her shoulders.  
She caught me in her long, slender arms,  
Kissed me with perfect sweetness,  
And softly said, “Dear heart, how do you like this?”

It was no dream; I lay fully awake.  
Yet all, through my gentleness, has turned  
Into a strange manner of forsaking.  
By her kindness, I am free to depart,  
And she is free to pursue novelty.  
But since I have been treated so kindly,  
I would gladly know what she has deserved.
outputs.L2:
Those who once pursued me now run away. Barefoot, they used to slip quietly through my room. Formerly they were mild, obedient, and affectionate; today they have grown untamed and seem to have forgotten how they once risked themselves to eat bread directly from my hand. Now they wander restlessly, always searching for something new.

I thank fortune that matters were far better on many occasions—perhaps twenty—but one encounter stands above the rest. Lightly dressed and looking alluring, a woman let her loose robe slide from her shoulders. She embraced me with her long, slender arms, kissed me tenderly, and whispered, “My darling, what do you think of this?”

This truly happened; I was lying there fully awake. Yet because I treated her gently, everything has changed into an unfamiliar kind of abandonment. Out of her generosity, she has granted me permission to leave, while she remains free to pursue each new desire. Since my kindness has been rewarded in this way, I would very much like to know what reward she herself deserves.
outputs.L3:
The speaker reflects bitterly on how those who once eagerly sought his company have now grown distant. Once gentle, familiar, and affectionate, they now seem wild and forgetful, as though their former intimacy had never existed. He remembers how completely they trusted him, approaching without fear and even taking bread directly from his hand.

Among these memories, one woman stands out with particular vividness. He recalls how her loose gown slipped from her shoulders as she took him in her arms and kissed him tenderly. The encounter felt unmistakably real, yet the woman has since abandoned him and turned elsewhere in search of novelty. Left behind, the speaker struggles to understand such a sudden change. With wounded pride and resentment, he asks what treatment she deserves for repaying his kindness and intimacy with rejection.
outputs.L4:
### “They Flee from Me” — Sir Thomas Wyatt

They flee from me that sometime did me seek  
With naked foot, stalking in my chamber.  
I have seen them gentle, tame, and meek,  
That now are wild and do not remember  
That sometime they put themselves in danger  
To take bread at my hand; and now they range,  
Busily seeking with a continual change.

Thankèd be fortune it hath been otherwise  
Twenty times better; but once in special,  
In thin array after a pleasant guise,  
When her loose gown from her shoulders did fall,  
And she me caught in her arms long and small;  
Therewithal sweetly did me kiss,  
And softly said, “Dear heart, how like you this?”

It was no dream: I lay broad waking.  
But all is turned, through my gentleness,  
Into a strange fashion of forsaking;  
And I have leave to go, of her goodness,  
And she also, to use newfangleness.  
But since that I so kindly am served,  
I would fain know what she hath deserved.
outputs.L5:
**They, With, That**

They arrived quietly, carrying stories with them—stories that had traveled across cities, oceans, and years. With every step, they drew closer to the place that had once felt like home. That was when they realized: belonging was not a destination, but the people who chose to walk beside them.
